{{short description|German mathematician}}
'''Britta Nestler''' (born 1972){{r|born}} is a German [[materials science|materials scientist]] at the [[Karlsruhe Institute of Technology]]. Her research involves the development of software to simulate the formation of microstructures in advanced materials for which experimental studies would be too expensive or difficult.{{r|physorg}}

Nestler did her undergraduate and graduate studies in mathematics and physics at [[RWTH Aachen University]]. She joined the [[Karlsruhe University of Applied Sciences]] in 2001 and moved to the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology in 2009.{{r|leibniz}}

In 2017, the [[Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft]] awarded to her the [[Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz Prize]] "for her significant, internationally recognised research in computer-assisted materials research and the development of new material models with multiscale and multiphysical approaches".{{r|leibniz}}
